text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS

- Argentinian President Carlos Saul Menem pledged in talks with visiting Hungarian President Arpad Goncz in Buenos Aires that Argentina will adopt a more flexible position than it has until now in the agricultural dispute with Hungary at the WTO.
- Finance Ministry State Secretary Laszlo Akar told MPs that GDP has increased and investment has become livelier, while macroeconomic indicators and Hungary's economy as a whole has stabilised.
- Parliament passed a bill on civilian alternative to military service.
- Parliament began debate Tuesday on a cabinet proposal to install a system of delegating deputies to social insurance authorities, rather than continuing the present system where they are elected.

- The Hungarian and Slovenian interior ministers are expected to sign an agreement in the summer whereby citizens of Hungary and Slovenia may cross between the two countries with only their personal identity cards.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. has restarted the transfer of property to local councils as compensation for inner city land used by privatised companies.
- Employees in the private sector earned a monthly gross HUF 52,130 on average in February, 22.8 percent up on a year earlier, the Central Statistical Office reports.
- The home savings institution Fundamenta Rt. is ready to start operation, said president and managing director Bela Barfai.
NEPSZABADSAG
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said on Tuesday it is not protection that Hungary seeks in joining NATO, but the benefits of belonging to an expanding zone of stability.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- A poll by the Gallup Institute last month shows that 47 percent of the public support Hungary's drive to join NATO.

- Managing Director of Financial Research Ltd Laszlo Lengyel charged that Hungary's economy was liberalised too early and without an adequate import duty policy. In addition, no other country has privatised its economy so quickly, with no one ever expecting such a dominant proportion of Hungary's economy to pass into foreign hands.

- The annual general meeting of EBRD beginning in London on Saturday, is expected to engage in debate on whether to reduce support to the more developed countries in Central and Eastern Europe, including Hungary.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn is due to visit Southeast Asia shortly, said Foreign Ministry spokesman Gabor Szentivanyi.
- Hungary has an unemployment level of around 9 percent, as compared to 10.9 percent in the EU, said Minister of Labour Peter Kiss.
- The state has brought in revenues of HUF 50 billion from privatisation in the catering sector, after selling nearly 90 percent of all properties.
- The Hungarian Oil and Gas Co. MOL is expected to dismiss a further 500 employees as part of a programme of staff cuts proposed by management in August.
